claims.text: A predictive model that incorporates defects and oxygen content will predict thermal conductivity more accurately than existing analytical methods in the 0–200 K regime.
A predictive model that incorporates defects and oxygen content will predict electrical conductivity more accurately than existing analytical methods in the 0–200 K regime.
A predictive model that incorporates defects and oxygen content will predict thermal conductivity more accurately than existing analytical methods in the 300–1200 K regime.
A predictive model that incorporates defects and oxygen content will predict electrical conductivity more accurately than existing analytical methods in the 300–1200 K regime.
The sample to which the prediction applies is bulk HfNbTaTiZr containing 1 wt.% oxygen.
Defects and oxygen atoms are present in the crystal lattice.
Defects and oxygen content alter phonon scattering.
Defects and oxygen content alter electron mobility.
Changes in phonon scattering affect thermal conductivity.
Changes in electron mobility affect electrical conductivity.
The new model may predict conductivity values approximately 10–20% higher than existing models.
Existing analytical predictions assume perfect, defect-free crystals.
The proposed model is applicable to bulk HfNbTaTiZr with 1 wt.% oxygen.
The model may not generalize to other alloy compositions or higher oxygen contents without validation.
Prediction improvement may vary with defect type and concentration.
A deviation greater than 15% between measured and newly predicted conductivity in either temperature regime is defined as falsifying the hypothesis.
